That the first safek was in its substance. This is according to R. Yochanan's explanation that I recalled in seif 8 ; regarding safek forbidden egg that became mixed even in a thousand, that all are forbidden ; for we do not consider double safek except in two mixtures, for then the safeks are equal; unlike here, where one safek is whether there is issur, and if you say there is issur, perhaps this is not it ; that double safek is like two substances; and in truth double safek must be in one substance of one matter, like two mixtures, or double safek whether there is issur here or not ; like a woman who committed adultery: safek under him, safek not under him, and if you say under him ; safek oness, safek willingly ; in the first chapter of Kesubos.
And behold in siman 57 regarding safek derusah that became mixed, that we do not permit by double safek in the name of R. Yochanan ; Beit Yosef wrote: I found written ; does R. Yochanan disagree with the Talmud, that we say double safek in d'oraisa? And he challenged ; behold even a certain derusah that became mixed is permitted from the Torah by majority, only d'rabbanan it is forbidden on account of davar sheb'minyan; if so, all absence in d'rabbanan safek and we should be lenient. And he answered on this: R. Yochanan deals where after the first safek arose the safek became known and it is full issur, and the name of certain issur applies to it ; thus according to what I wrote there is no challenge at all, for here is different from other double safek as I mentioned; and also the second challenge is not difficult at all, for there is no Torah permission in the substance of the issur itself, only through nullification in the majority, and the Sages said wherever there is an important item nullification in the majority does not help.
I found again so in Darkei Moshe ; on account of this he wrote to be lenient, etc. ; see there.
It is issur d'oraisa, etc. ; see what I wrote in siman 66 seif 4 in the hagahah, that from this it appears to me Rama decided there that egg blood is d'rabbanan when mixtures were made.
And I saw in a newly printed book of Maharar Binyamin, who wrote in responsum siman 37, to bring proof that according to R. Yochanan there is no issur in double safek that is not in one substance ; rather one safek in its substance and the second through mixtures ; except specifically when known at intervals ; from what Rashba wrote that Beit Yosef brought in this siman, and these are his words: how can you say perhaps this is not it, and if you say this is it, perhaps that safek was permitted ; behold you already forbade it from safek that fell in its substance, and after you forbid it how can you return and permit it, end of his words; and he means: since it was already known and forbidden before it became mixed ; behold if it was not known and forbidden before it became mixed, we permit by double safek; and it is not clear to my humble opinion, for this was caused by the citation that Beit Yosef copied from Terumat HaDeshen the long version ; and in truth Beit Yosef abbreviated in his citation, for there daf 115 he wrote: and in my humble opinion it is difficult against R. Yochanan that he only permitted double safek of two mixtures from the first chapter of Kesubos ; safek under her she committed adultery, safek not under her, and if you say under her ; perhaps by oness, and it is double safek; and behold the safeks are not on account of mixtures, and nevertheless we say double safek to be lenient; and one may say there it is different, for it cannot come before you except through two safeks, and you cannot be stringent and say how can you permit when you already forbade, as you say regarding safek egg laid on Yom Tov that immediately it stood in prohibition for us and afterward became mixed ; see there and investigate.
But if there were two safeks, etc., and both safeks became known, etc. ; the Rav copied this from Hagahot Issur VeHeter at the end of the book, who wrote, and these are his words: and the same applies if the two safeks were complete double safek ; that is, in one matter and in one substance ; nevertheless it is not permitted thereby unless they come at one time; but if the first safek became known first, count that time as certain issur, and when the second safek comes, even without mixtures, there is only one safek, end of his words; and I did not understand these words at all ; for since he said "unless they come at one time," this implies that sometimes it is possible they do not come at one time ; and how can you find that it becomes known between the first safek and the second safek in double safek when they are in one substance and one matter, such as in the safek "under him she committed adultery" and safek oness mentioned above ; for one cannot say the first safek became known before the second became known; and if you wish to say that at first they noticed the first safek and did not notice the second safek, and when they notice it the matter is revealed retroactively that it was never forbidden ; behold no new matter was born for us, only knowledge was lacking ; and in Rama's words there is somewhat room to force and explain that he says thus: whenever both safeks became known specifically together, this is a sign of double safek that is proper ; for in double safek in two substances it is possible to become known at intervals. And so I saw in a responsum of Maharar Binyamin z"l, who wrote that one should not heed this hagahah, for it is plain that in double safek through two mixtures it is permitted even when known at intervals, and he brought proper proof for this ; automatically the same applies in double safek if there is issur here. The general rule emerging in double safek is thus: whenever the first safek is forbidden because it is important and is not nullified in the majority ; even though the essence of the issur is rabbinic, such as safek egg born on Yom Tov that afterward became mixed ; double safek does not help in it, since the safeks are not in one matter; rather we require that both safeks be through mixtures; and "known at intervals" neither adds nor subtracts anything from double safek. And likewise if there are two safeks whether there is issur here entirely ; then it helps in all cases; only there is a distinction in double safek through mixtures ; that if it is certain issur and it is important, we require three mixtures, as I wrote in seif 8; but if safek issur became mixed, we require only two mixtures and there is double safek to be lenient:
There is room to permit by double safek, etc. ; I saw in this a dispute of Baalei Karnayim ; that is Issur VeHeter, and on him the author of Darkei Moshe and Turei Chayim klal 43 seif 7, and on him in responsum Masat Binyamin siman 38 ; and in all their words I wonder, as I will explain: Issur VeHeter klal 26 din 2 wrote: one who slaughters with a checked knife and after shechitah the knife is found damaged and afterward became mixed among other animals ; one may not permit by double safek, perhaps it is not this one, and if you find to say that it is this one, perhaps it was slaughtered properly ; for we conclude in the Gemara: an animal while alive stands in presumption of issur ; therefore there is only one safek, perhaps it is not this one ; for if you say it is this one, perhaps it was slaughtered properly ; for whatever is safek we forbid it because of presumption it was certainly issur and not safek ; and therefore one may not permit by double safek except where there is no presumption of issur ; when you say "if you say" you cannot establish it on presumption of issur, like this open door that I found at the beginning of Kesubos ; "if you say" "under him" there is no establishing presumption of issur beforehand, etc., end of his words. And he wrote on this in Darkei Moshe and Turei Chayim that this is not correct ; for Rashba wrote in responsum siman 401 that double safek helps even where there is presumption of issur; and so it appears from the laws of safek derusah that became mixed ; for if not for the reason that the first safek was in its substance, there would be double safek ; and we would permit even though it had presumption of issur of limb from a living creature, end of his words. And so too here in Shulchan Aruch ; and Maharar Binyamin mentioned disagrees with him on Rama, and wrote that there is no proof from safek derusah ; for there presumption of issur of limb from a living creature helps only regarding safek that occurred because of shechitah, but not regarding issur that does not depend on shechitah ; and he elaborated to explain this matter. And according to him safek derusah where the safek was born from life will be permitted ; for it is like the case where a wolf took, etc. ; for there is no presumption of issur, and we say in it "it was slaughtered, it is permitted" ; and Tosafot's words in chapter 4 of Achin (Yevamos daf 30) escaped him, who wrote, and these are his words: and in the first chapter of Chullin we say: an animal while alive stands in presumption of issur, etc. was slaughtered, it is permitted etc. it appears specifically for a defect born after shechitah it was in presumption of heter, such as a wolf came and took its innards, etc. ; but if the safek was born from life, such as safek derusah ; not because at the hour the safek was born it was still in presumption of issur end of his words ; behold before you that presumption of issur of limb from a living creature helps for safek derusah ; and if so Rama properly brings proof from safek derusah regarding double safek, that we see in it that it helps if it is possible to say so; but we do not care in this what was at first in presumption of issur of the living limb ; even though it helped to forbid in one safek ; rather I see that regarding the halachah all were correct, as I will explain ; it is stated in responsum of Rashba siman 401, and these are his words: I see wonder in the matters you asked regarding double safek where issur was presumed, like Kesubos ; how is issur presumed? For there is only safek of one corpse that was lost ; and if you call it "issur was presumed," every mixed item that we presumed in issur because of its mixture ; behold your question is explained from a ring of gentiles, etc., end of his words ; and he brings on this many proofs; and afterward wrote: and do not answer me from Rav Huna in the first chapter of Chullin ; he checked the knife and slaughtered, and it was found spoiled ; behold this is forbidden, lest it was spoiled in the skin; and an incident occurred with thirteen animals and they forbade even the first ; learn from this that double safek is forbidden, for he follows his own view that an animal while alive stands in presumption of issur, etc.; and know further that double safek is preferable to majority, and it is possible its permission is stronger than majority ; for in lineage one is disqualified by one majority and qualified by double safek; and just as we follow majority to permit in all Torah prohibitions, even where presumption of issur was established, such as a piece of issur that became mixed in two of heter ; the same applies to double safek that it is permitted, even where presumption of issur was established, end of his words. And it appears difficult what he wrote in that case of Rav Huna that he mentioned first ; that we follow presumption of issur and double safek does not help ; and what is different from that which he wrote afterward that we follow double safek even where presumption of issur was established; and if you investigate you will find that Rashba distinguishes in that presumption of issur of Rav Huna ; that an animal while alive stands in presumption of issur until you know it was slaughtered properly; and end ; since the doubt afterward is in shechitah itself whether it was done properly, and to remove it from presumption that it was not slaughtered, double safek does not help ; since in that issur itself from which it had not certainly departed; but if the presumption of issur is because of double safek ; that is, it had presumption of limb from a living animal and was slaughtered properly, only there is doubt because of double safek, such as it became mixed first and afterward became mixed in other mixtures ; certainly double safek helps; and so all other issur, such as a piece of chelev that became mixed in two mixtures ; for Rashba explicitly compared double safek to majority in this way; and it follows from our words that Rama did not challenge Issur VeHeter at all ; for Issur VeHeter forbade only in safek shechitah, and that which Rashba mentioned, that case of Rav Huna ; there certainly double safek does not help for the reason I mentioned; and also Maharar Binyamin ; it appears to me ; disagreed with Rama as we mentioned, and said double safek does not help where presumption of issur was established; he ruled well on his question that deals also with safek shechitah ; only it appears he wants to rule thus in every double safek where presumption of issur was established, even in a safek not regarding shechitah ; for he wrote against Rama that he has no proof from Rashba's words siman 401 ; for there in siman 401 he does not speak of presumption of issur, as Rashba wrote explicitly in responsum that where there was full presumption, double safek does not help; rather it deals with presumption of safek issur, such as safek challal in Kesubos; and according to the questioner's view they called presumption of issur as explained there, and on this he wrote to permit; but with full presumption of issur, like this case of Rav Huna, double safek does not help ; until here is his language; and may he rest in honor ; for he did not investigate Rashba's words well, because he did not see the end of the matter ; for Rashba wrote explicitly at the end "and know further," etc., as I mentioned; it is clear that even with full presumption of issur it helps; and from the outset he wrote plainly that that presumption of issur that the questioner called presumption of issur ; that is, from the side of mixtures ; obviously it helps; and he concluded that even with full presumption of issur, such as a piece of chelev, double safek helps in it like majority, and we do not say it does not help except in that case of Rav Huna where the doubt is in shechitah, as I mentioned; and the Rav Maharar Binyamin understood in Rashba that every presumption of issur is like that of Rav Huna ; and it is not so. What emerges from our words for the halachah: even in every issur certainly double safek helps to permit if it does not contradict the presumption itself ; like safek in shechitah, that if double safek helps in it, it would contradict the presumption that it was not slaughtered but limb from a living animal ; in this we say it does not help; and similar to this is a woman who is in presumption of married woman and afterward safeks arose regarding her husband's death or divorce ; even if there were several double safeks they would not help, since you come to remove her from the category of married woman that she was first, and you come to contradict it directly; but in other presumption of issur where safeks for permission arose from another side, such as from mixtures ; certainly double safeks help to remove from issur, for from the outset there is nothing here that contradicts one another; and therefore in safek derusah, if there was full double safek, it well helps to nullify presumption of issur of limb from a living animal that the innards call thus ; it appears to me clear and correct in this:
What emerges from our words for the halachah: that even in every case of certain issur, double safek [sefek sefeika] is effective to permit ; provided it does not contradict the chazakah itself. For example in the safek of shechitah: if double safek were effective there, it would negate the chazakah that the animal was presumed to be unslaughtered ; that is, it would have the status of a limb from a living animal; in that case we say double safek is not effective. Similarly, a woman who has the chazakah of being a married woman and subsequently doubts arose about the death of her husband or her divorce ; even if there were several instances of double safek they would not be effective, since you are coming to remove her from the category of married woman that she had initially, and you are coming to directly negate it. But in other cases of a presumptive issur where doubts arose regarding a permissive outcome from a different direction ; such as through a mixture ; double safek certainly is effective to remove it from the initial issur, for there is no element here that contradicts one thing with the other. Therefore in the case of safek derusah, if there were a full double safek, it is properly effective to nullify the presumptive issur of eiver min hachai from the outset ; so it appears to my humble opinion, clearly and correctly.
See above in siman 53. Explanation: that there he is stringent regarding what slipped out ; and see what I wrote there.

baer_heitev.he:
בגופו. פי' הש"ך דל"ד לב' תערובות דתערובות הב' מותר מכח ס"ס דהתם הספק הא' לא היה בגופו רק בתערובות משא"כ כאן דהספק הא' היה בגופו (ר"ל בגוף האיסור שמא לאו טריפה וספק הב' הוא שמא לא זהו שאכל) אבל קשה דהטור והרשב"א והפוסקים לא הוצרכו לזה אלא לשיטתם דס"ל דתערובות הב' מותר אבל המחבר דס"ל בס"ח דתערובות הב' אסור א"כ אפילו לא היה ספק הראשון בגופו אסור ס"ס שנתערב דלא יהא אלא ב' תערובות וצ"ע (ולי נראה דל"ק מידי דלעיל בס"ח מיירי מדבר חשוב שאינו בטל לכך פסק המחבר דבעינן ג' תערובות דבתערובות הראשון לא שייך לומר חד בתרי בטל וכאן מיירי מדברים שאינם חשובים ובטלים לכך א"צ אלא ב' תערובות ודוק) והט"ז כ' דבאמת צריך שיהא ס"ס בגוף א' מענין א' כמו ב' תערובות או ס"ס אם יש כאן איסור או לא כמו באשה שזינתה ספק תחתיו ספק אינה תחתיו ואת"ל תחתיו ספק באונס ספק ברצון ולמ"ש המחבר כאן דאין מתירין מכח ס"ס מיירי אפי' לא נודע בנתיים עכ"ל:
ס"ס. כתבו הט"ז וש"ך אפילו לא נודע הספק הראשון רק עד אחר שנתערב כגון שנתערבו כמה ביצים ביחד ואח"כ נודע ספק טריפה בתרנגולת וא"כ ב' הספיקות באין כא' מ"מ כיון שהספק הראשון מן התורה לא הוי ס"ס ואם נתחלפה גבינה שאינה ידוע אם היא גבינת ישראל או גבינת עובד כוכבים דבכה"ג הוי ספק דרבנן ולחומרא כדלקמן להמחבר אינה בטלה בתערובות אף שהספק הראשון הוא מדרבנן כיון שהוא בגופו ולהר"ב בהג"ה בטל כיון שהספק הראשון אינו מן התורה א"כ הוי ס"ס מיהו אפשר דמר אמר חדא ומר אמר חדא ולא פליגי ולא בא הר"ב אלא להוסיף דבס"ס אם יש כאן איסור כלל מותר אפילו בגופו של איסור ועי' בתשובת ן' לב ח"ג סי' ק' עכ"ל:
ביחד. כתב הט"ז דדברים אלו תמוהין דמשמע שאפשר דלפעמים לא יבואו הספיקות בפעם א' וזה א"א למצוא שיהא נודע בין ספק א' לספק ב' בס"ס שהם בגוף א' וענין אחד כגון בספק זינתה תחתיו וספק אונס דאין שייך לומר דנודע הספק הא' קודם שנודע הב' ובדברי רמ"א יש קצת לדחוק ולפרש דה"ק כל שנודע ב' הספיקות דוקא ביחד זהו סימן לס"ס שהוא כראוי דאלו בס"ס בשני גופים אפשר להיות נודע בנתיים וכן ראיתי בתשובה למהר"ר בנימין ז"ל שכ' שאין להשגיח בהג"ה זאת כי פשוט הוא שבס"ס שע"י שני תערובות מותר אפילו נודע בנתיים ממילא ה"ה בס"ס אם יש כאן איסור. כלל העולה בס"ס הוא כן. דכל שהספק הא' הוא אסור מצד שהוא חשוב ואינו בטל ברוב שאע"פ שעיקר האיסור הוא מדרבנן כמו ספק ביצה שנולדה ביו"ט ושוב נתערבה לא מהני בה ס"ס כיון שאין הספיקות בענין א' אלא בעינן שיהיו ב' הספיקות ע"י תערובות ונודע בנתיים לא מעלה ולא מוריד בשום דבר מהס"ס וכן אם יש ב' ספיקות אם יש כאן איסור לגמרי אז מהני בכל גווני רק שיש חילוק בס"ס שע"י תערובות שאם הוא איסור ודאי והוא חשוב בעינן ג' תערובות וכמ"ש בס"ח אבל אם הספק איסור נתערב לא בעינן רק ב' תערובות והוא ס"ס ולהקל עכ"ל:
וע"ל. ושם מחמיר בנשמט וכ' הט"ז מדברי הרב משמע אפי' אם שחט בסכין בדוק ולאחר שחיטה נמצא פגום ונתערבה אח"כ בין בהמות אחרות דיש להתיר מכח ס"ס שמא אינה זאת ואת"ל שהיא זאת שמא נשחטה כדינה ואע"ג שהיתה קודם שחיט' בחזקת איסור כן משמעות הרמ"א והוא חולק ע"ז ופסק דבספק שחיטה יש לאסור כיון שהספק הוא אח"כ בשחיטה עצמה אם נעשית כראוי ולהוציאה מחזקת שלא נשחטה אין מועיל ס"ס כיון דבאותו איסור עצמו שהיה קודם לא יצאה ממנו בודאי אבל אם החזקה של איסור מחמת ד"א דהיינו שהיה לו חזקת אמ"ה ונשחט כראוי רק שיש ספק מחמת דבר אחר כגון שנתערב תחלה ואח"כ נתערב בתערובת אחר ודאי מהני ס"ס וכן כל שאר איסור כגון חתיכת חלב שנתערבה בשני תערובות מותר מכח ס"ס. כלל העולה מדברינו להלכה דאפילו בכל איסור ודאי מהני ס"ס להתיר אם אינו סותר את החזקה עצמה כההיא דספק בשחיטה דאם מועיל בה הס"ס תסתור החזקה שהיתה בחזקת שאינה שחוטה אלא אמ"ה בזה אמרינן דלא מועיל ודומה לזה האשה שהיא בחזקת אשת איש ונולדו אח"כ ספיקות במיתת הבעל או בגירושין אפילו הוי כמה ספיקות לא יועילו כיון שאתה בא להוציאה מחזקת א"א שהיתה תחלה ואתה בא לסותרה ממש אבל בשאר חזקת איסור שנולדו ספיקות להתיר מצד אחר כגון מצד התערובות ודאי מועילים ס"ס להוציאו מן האיסור דמתחלה דאין כאן דבר הסותר זא"ז וע"כ בספק דרוסה אם היה ס"ס גמור שפיר מועיל לבטל חזקת האיסור דאמ"ה דמעיקרא כנ"ל ברור ונכון בזה עכ"ל:
baer_heitev.en:
"**In its substance.**" The Shach wrote — some say that for two mixtures, the second mixtures are permitted by force of double safek, for there the first doubt was not in its substance but only in mixtures; unlike here, where the first doubt was in its substance (meaning, in the substance of the issur — lest it is not tereifah — and the second doubt is lest this is not what he ate). But it is difficult — for the Tur and Rashba and the poskim did not need this except according to their view that the second mixtures are permitted; but the Mechaber, who holds in seif 8 that the second mixtures are forbidden — if so, even if the first doubt were not in its substance, a forbidden double safek when mixed would require only two mixtures — requires study (and to me it appears there is no question at all — for above in seif 8 it deals with an important thing that is not nullified, therefore the Mechaber ruled that we require three mixtures, for in the first mixture it is not proper to say one in two is nullified; and here it deals with things that are not important and are nullified, therefore only two mixtures are required — investigate). And the Taz wrote that in truth there must be double safek in one substance, one matter — like two mixtures — or double safek whether there is issur here or not, like a woman who committed adultery: doubt whether she was underneath, doubt whether she was not underneath; and if you say she was underneath — doubt whether by force or willingly. And regarding what the Mechaber wrote here that one does not permit by force of double safek — it deals even if it was not known simultaneously; end of his words.
"**Double safek.**" The Taz and Shach wrote that even if the first doubt was not known until after it became mixed — such as several eggs became mixed together, and afterward a doubt of tereifah in the poultry became known — and if so, the two doubts do not come as one; nevertheless, since the first doubt is from the Torah, it is not double safek. And if cheese was exchanged and it is not known whether it is cheese of a Jew or cheese of a non-Jew — in such a case it is a d'rabbanan doubt, and for stringency, as below for the Mechaber, it is not nullified in mixtures, even though the first doubt is d'rabbanan, since it is in its substance. And for the Rama in the hagahah — it is nullified, since the first doubt is not from the Torah; if so, it is double safek. However, it is possible that one master said one thing and one master said another, and they do not disagree; and the Rama did not come except to add that with double safek, if there is any issur here at all, it is permitted even in the substance of issur; and see in the responsum of Noda Biyehuda, vol. 3, siman 100; end of his words.
"**Together.**" The Taz wrote that these matters are astonishing — for it appears that sometimes the doubts do not come at once, and this is impossible to find, that it should be known between doubt one and doubt two in double safek when they are in one substance and one matter — such as in the doubt whether she committed adultery underneath and the doubt of force; for it is not proper to say that the first doubt was known before the second became known. And in the words of the Rama there is somewhat to strain and explain that this is what he means: only when both doubts are known specifically together — this is a sign of double safek that is proper; unlike double safek in two substances, where it is possible to be known simultaneously. And likewise I saw in a responsum to Maharar Binyamin, and these are his words, that one should not heed this hagahah — for it is plain that in double safek through two mixtures it is permitted even if known simultaneously; the same is true of double safek whether there is issur here. The general principle rising from double safek is thus: that whenever the first doubt is forbidden because it is important and is not nullified in the majority — even though the main issur is d'rabbanan, such as a doubtful egg born on Yom Tov and then became mixed — double safek does not help in it, since the doubts are not one matter; rather, we require that the two doubts come through mixtures — and known simultaneously does not raise or lower anything of the double safek. And likewise, if there are two doubts whether there is issur here entirely — then it helps in all manners; only there is a difference in double safek through mixtures — that if it is a certain issur and it is important, we require three mixtures, as he wrote in seif 8; but if a doubtful issur became mixed, we require only two mixtures, and it is double safek to be lenient; end of his words.
"**And see there.**" And there he is stringent regarding that which became dislodged. And the Taz wrote that from the Rav's words it appears that even if he slaughtered with a checked knife and after slaughter a defect was found and it became mixed afterward among other animals — there is room to permit by force of double safek: perhaps it is not this one; and if you say it is this one — perhaps it was slaughtered properly; and even though before slaughter it was in presumption of issur — such is the implication of the Rama; and he disagrees on this and ruled that in a doubt of slaughter one must forbid, since the doubt is afterward in the slaughter itself whether it was done properly; and to remove it from presumption of non-slaughter, double safek does not help — since from that issur itself that was before, it certainly did not exit from it. But if the presumption of issur is because of another reason — that is, that it had presumption of a live animal and was slaughtered properly, only there is doubt because of another matter, such as that it became mixed first and afterward became mixed in another mixture — certainly double safek helps. And likewise all other issur, such as a piece of milk that became mixed in two mixtures — permitted by force of double safek. The general principle rising from our words for the halachah: that even in every certain issur, double safek helps to permit if it does not contradict the presumption itself — like that case of a doubt in slaughter, for if double safek helps in it, it would contradict the presumption that it was in presumption of non-slaughter but a live animal; in this we say it does not help. And similar to this is the woman who is in presumption of a married woman, and afterward doubts arose in the death of the husband or in divorce — even if there are several doubts, they will not help, since you come to remove her from presumption of a married woman that was first, and you come to contradict it directly. But in other presumption of issur where doubts arose to permit from another side — such as from the side of mixtures — certainly double safek helps to remove it from the issur, for initially there is nothing here that contradicts one another. And until here — in a doubt of one that was gored, if there were a complete double safek, it properly helps to nullify the presumption of the issur of a live animal, as explained initially — it appears to me clear and correct in this; end of his words.

beur_hagra.he:
ספק כו' וי"א כו'. כנ"ל וכ"ז לשיטת התוס' ורשב"א אבל להרמב"ם בלא"ה תערובת הראשון ודאי יחשב כנ"ל:
(ליקוט) ספק כו'. ור"ת חולק על זה ומפרש ההיא דריש י"ט דאודאה קאי וכנ"ל וער"ש פ"ג דערלה ריש מתני' ו' נתערבה באחרות כו' וכ' בת"ה שבירושלמי שם משמע כדברי ר"ת דאודאה קאי דגרסינן שם נתערבה א' במאה או א' באלף כולן אסורות ובעי שם מה כמ"ד ספק הכן אסור כו' ומשני נשרים ספק מהיום נשרו ספק מאתמול ברם הכא יש כאן אחת אסורה והיא מוכחת על כולן אלמא בודאי מיירי ע"ש ומ"מ הסכים לדברי ר"י ממ"ש בזבחים שם דדוקא לתרי והוא דאיכא רובא אבל בלא"ה לא ואע"ג דכל חד הוא בס"ס אלא דכל שאסור ד"ת לא אמרינן ס"ס להקל ע"ש קט"ז א' (ע"ש היטב) ועבהג"ה (ע"כ):
אבל אם כו'. כמ"ש בכתובות פ' א' ושאר מקומות:
ונודעו כו'. כ"כ או"ה וצ"ע דא"כ כל שקלא וטריא דריש י"ט ואם נתערבה כו' פי' ר"ת ור"י בכדי והא מיתוקם שפיר בנודעה שכן פשטא דברייתא:
אע"פ כו'. בתוס' דע"ז ל"ח ב' ד"ה אי כו' וה"ט לפי שהוא ס"ס כו' וכ' הרא"ש שם סי' ל"ח וא"ת וליטעמיה קפילא וי"ל כיון דס"ס הוא לא הטריחוהו חכמים כו' וכמ"ש בנדה ס"ו א' ותבדוק כו' ועתוס' שם ד"ה ותבדוק כו' ור"ת כו' ויש להעמיד כו' ופי' סמ"ג דה"ק בגמ' לפי שאין כל כו' ועצה טובה קמ"ל דהשתא מותרת בלא בדיקה משום ס"ס שמא אינו מן המקור ואת"ל מן המקור שמא לא יבא בבעל שני דלא כל האצבעות שוות משא"כ כשתבדוק שיתברר שבא מן המקור ותאסר לשני וכ"כ כל הפוסקים ועב"י סי' קפ"ד:
beur_hagra.en:
A doubt, etc., and some say, etc., as noted — and all of this is according to Tosafot's and the Rashba's view; but for the Rambam, without this, the first mixture is considered definite, as noted:
(Collected notes) A doubt, etc. And R' Tam disagrees with this and explains that [passage] at the beginning of Yevamot as dealing with a definite case, as noted; and see R' Shmuel, chapter 3 of Orlah, beginning of the mishnah, 6 — "it was mixed with others," etc. And he wrote in Terumat HaDeshen that in the Yerushalmi there it appears like the words of R' Tam, that it deals with a definite case — for we have the version there: "it was mixed, one in a hundred or one in a thousand — all are forbidden," and it asks there: what, according to the one who says that a doubt is thus forbidden, etc., and it answers: "eagles — a doubt whether they fell today, a doubt whether from yesterday" — but here there is one forbidden item here and it is proven regarding all of them; which shows that it deals with a definite case — see there. Nevertheless he agreed to the words of R' Yitzchak from what is written in Zevachim there — that specifically for two, and that is when there is a majority; but without this, no. And even though each one is a safek safeka, rather that whatever is forbidden by Torah law we do not say safek safeka to be lenient — see there, Ketubot 16a (see there well), and in the hagahah (end of passage).
But if, etc. As written in Kesubos chapter 1 and other places.
And they became known, etc. So too Issur VeHeter — and this requires study, for if so, all the give-and-take at the beginning of Yevamot, "and if it was mixed," etc. — R' Tam and R' Yitzchak explain as b'chedi; but behold, it resolves well as "it became known," for such is the plain meaning of the baraisa.
Even though, etc. In Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 38b, s.v. i, etc., "and the reason is because it is safek safeka," etc., and the Rosh wrote there siman 38, "and if you ask — according to his reasoning it is doubled; one can say that since it is safek safeka they did not trouble him," etc., and as written in Niddah 66a, "and she should examine," etc., and Tosafot there, s.v. vetivdok, etc., and R' Tam, etc., "and one can establish," etc., and Semag explains that this is what the Gemara means: because there is no, etc., "good advice" — it teaches us that now it is permitted without examination because of safek safeka, lest it is not from the source; and if you say from the source, lest it will not come in a second husband — for not all fingers are equal — which is not so when she examines, that it will be clarified that it came from the source and she will be forbidden to a second [husband]. And so too all the poskim, and in Beit Yosef siman 184.

peleti.he:
משום דספק א' וכו' הקשה הש"ך כיון דמחבר ס"ל כרמב"ם דבעינן שלשה תערובת דהיינו ג' ספיקות ובזה בטריפה שנתערב הוא רק ב' תערובת דהיינו ב' ספיקות. ולפמש"ל לק"מ דוקא בדבר חשוב שאין מתבטל כלל בעינן ג' ספיקות אבל ספק טריפה הוא מדבר מתבטל ואין חשוב וסגי בב' ספיקות ולכך נתן טעם דהוי ספק א' בגופו:
אין להתירו ודעת ר"ת להתיר ס"ס כי האי ועיין פר"ח דף מ"ו דכתב דעת בעל התרומה מסכים לחד תי' של רשב"א אפילו ספק תערובת חד בחד ומיקרי ג"כ ס"ס לדעת ר"ת. רש לדקדק הא דאמרינן כריתות דף טו"ב בתוס' ד"ה מדסיפא כו' דכתבו ואשמועינן דאפילו בס"ס ספק שומן ספק חלב ואת"ל חלב ואת"ל חלב דלמא לא כשיעור מייתי אשם תלוי. ויש להבין למה באמת מייתי אשם תלוי הא ה"ל ס"ס ומועיל בכל התורה ואי דהך חלב או שומן הוי רק חד בחד מה בכך הא מועיל לשיטת ר"ת. וכן קשה הא דאמרינן גיטין ונזיר האומר לשלוחו צא וקדש לי אשה ולא נודע אסור בכל הנשים דלמא קידש קרובתה וקשה הא איכא ע"ס דילמא לא קידש שליח כלל שום אשה ואת"ל קידש דילמא לאו קרובת אשה שרוצה להנשא היא. בשלמא לר"י לא דמיין הספיקות משא"כ לר"ת קשה וצ"ע: אמנם אי נימא דר"ת ס"ל ג"כ דבעינן ס"ס מתהפך יש ליישב דשם בנזיר ל"ל איפכ' ספק לא קידש קרובת זה ואת"ל קידש דילמא לא קידש כלל זה א"א דהא אמרת אפילו קרובתה קידש. וכן בהך ספק אכל ג"כ י"ל בזה אופן היה כאן חתיכה שומן ואין בה זית וחתיכה א' חלב ויש בו כזית ועוד חתיכה בלתי כזית ואכל א' מג' והשאר לאבדו וא"כ כאן ספק אי אכל חלב או שומן וגם אם אכל חלב אי מאותו שיש בו כזית או אין בו כזית והוה ס"ס אבל אינו מתהפך לומר ספק לא אכל ואת"ל אכל זית דילמא שומן זה א"א דהא שומן לא היה בו כזית. וזה ס"ס שכוון עליו תוס' דמחייב אשם תלוי כיון דאינו מתהפך ומה שהקשה הב"ש בא"ע וכן מפורסם הקו' בשם הגאון מהור"ר הילמ"ן ז"ל דמו"ש מפראג מהא דאלמנת עיסה דאיירי דהי' ספק בן ט' לראשון בן ז' לאחרון דהי' חלל דמתיר ר"י משום דהוי ס"ס דילמא לא הי' כל התערובות פסולה ואת"ל דהי' דילמא מן ראשון הא ס"ס ס' בגופו וס' בתערובת צ"ל שאני דהתם אלמנה יש לה חזק' כשרות ובתה באמת פסול ואע"ג דתו' כתבו כתובות י"ד ד"ה אלמנה עיסה וכו' דלכך הבת פסול לא מדינא רק מעלה עשו ביוחסין זהו כתבו לשיטת ר"ת דמכשיר כל הני ס"ס. אבל לשיטת ר"י דחולק באמת הבת מדינא פסול דל"ל ס"ס כלל והא דס"ל לר"י בביצת ספק טריפה שנתערבה באלף דלא מהני ס"ס הנ"ל דהוי ספק אחד בגופו וספק אחד וכו' אף דיש לביצה חזקת היתר דאינו טריפה. י"ל דמיירי כפי' רש"י שם דיש כאן שני תרנגולת אחת כשרה ואחת טריפה ודאי והטילו ביצה ולא ידענו ממי יצא הביצה א"כ לא שייך כאן חזקת היתר דהא לא נודע ממי נולדה אם מטריפה או מכשרה. ולפי אותו סברה שכתב רמ"א הואיל וספק ראשון מהתורה וכו' י"ל ה"מ לדעת רשב"א ור"ן דכל ספק איסור מהתורה אסור אם כן שפיר י"ל דאין לצרפו לכלל ספיקות דתערובות אבל אי אינו אסור רק מדרבנן א"כ מה בכך שספק ראשון אסור מהתורה זהו גופו לאסור הוא דרבנן. והנה הרשב"א והר"ן תירץ לדעתו דספק מהתורה אסור למה ספק ממזר ושתוקי מותר מהתורה דביוחסין הקילה התורה לפ"ז י"ל אף ספק חלל בכלל דלא עדיף מספק ממזר וא"כ דמהתורה ספיקו מותר שפיר מצטרף ספק זה לספק דתערובת וס"ל ספק ספיקא ולא דמי כלל לשאר ספיקא דספקן אסור מהתורה וק"ל:
ספק ספיקא והנה הפר"ח הביא דעת רבינו דס"ל באיסור דרבנן מודה ר"י לר"ת והקשה הפר"ח הא ר"י ס"ל גבי ביצה דקתני ספקו אסורה ונתערבה באלף אספק קאי ולא אודאי ומכח זה חולק על ר"ת דס"ל ספק בגופו וכו' אמרינן א"כ במסקנא דמוקמינן בנולדה ביו"ט גרידא ואינו רק איסור דרבנן. ומ"מ קתני נתערבה וכו' ש"מ דאפילו באיסור דרבנן לא אמרינן ספק בגופו וכו'. ולא ידעתי מה חרי הגדול הזה בשלמא אי איירי בספק טריפה ס"ל לר"י דלא יתכן לומר אם נתערבה באלף אודאי טריפה ודאי טריפה מאן דכר שמי' הלא אין זכר בברייתא כלל מודאי טריפה עד שיתכן עליו הלשון ואם נתערבה וכו' וע"כ עלה דקתני וספקה דהיינו ספק טריפה אסורה עלה קאי ואם נתערבה וצדקו דברי ר"י אבל אי איירי בביצה שנולדה ביו"ט שפיר י"ל ואם נתערבה אודאי נולדה ביו"ט קאי דהא הברייתא מתחיל בביצה שנולדה ביו"ט וכו' ושפיר קאי עלה דאם הך ביצה דהתחיל בה הברייתא והיינו שנולדה ביו"ט שנתערב באלף ולק"מ דעל ודאי קאי אבל בספק ה"ל ס"ס ומותר ולק"מ:
peleti.en:
Because of one safek, etc. — Shach challenged: since the Mechaber holds like Rambam that we require three mixtures — that is, three safeks — and here in tereifah that became mixed there are only two mixtures — that is, two safeks. And as I wrote — requires study — specifically regarding an important item that is not nullified at all we require three safeks; but safek of tereifah is from something nullifiable and is not important, and two safeks suffice; therefore he gave a reason that it is one safek in itself.
One may not permit it — and Rabbeinu Tam's view is to permit double safek like this; and see Pri Chadash daf 46 that wrote the author of Terumat HaDeshen agrees to one answer of Rashba — even safek of mixture one in one is also called double safek according to Rabbeinu Tam. Rashba investigated this that we say in Kerisos daf 15 side 2 in Tosafot s.v. "from the end," etc. that they wrote and inform us that even with double safek — safek fat safek milk, and if you say milk and if you say milk — perhaps not the requisite amount — he brings a provisional guilt offering. And one must understand: why in truth does he bring a provisional guilt offering — behold this is double safek and helps in the entire Torah; and if this milk or fat is only one in one — what of it — it helps according to Rabbeinu Tam's view. And likewise it is difficult this that we say in Gittin and Nazir: one who says to his agent "Go and betroth a wife for me" and it is not known — he is forbidden to all women — perhaps he betrothed his relative; and it is difficult — behold there are ten safeks — perhaps the agent did not betroth any woman at all, and if you say he betrothed — perhaps she is not the relative of the woman he wishes to marry. Granted for R' Yochanan the safeks are not comparable — unlike for Rabbeinu Tam it is difficult — requires study. However, if we say Rabbeinu Tam also holds we require reversible double safek — one can resolve: there in Nazir why need reverse safek — perhaps he did not betroth a relative — this; and if you say he betrothed — perhaps he did not betroth at all — this is impossible, for you said even if he betrothed his relative. And likewise in that safek of eating too one can say in this manner: there was here a piece of fat with no olive-size and one piece of milk with an olive-size and another piece less than olive-size — and he ate one of three and the rest were lost — if so here safek whether he ate milk or fat, and also if he ate milk whether from that which has olive-size or does not have olive-size — and it is double safek; but it is not reversible to say safek he did not eat and if you say he ate olive-size — perhaps this is fat — this is impossible, for the fat did not have olive-size. And this is the double safek Tosafot intended regarding obligating a provisional guilt offering — since it is not reversible. And what Beit Shmuel challenged in Even HaEzer, and likewise the difficulty is well known in the name of the gaon Maharal Hilman and these are his words from Prague — from this of the widow of dough that deals with that there was safek a nine-month son to the first, a seven-month son to the last who was a challal — R' Yochanan permits because it is double safek — perhaps the entire mixture was invalid, and if you say it was — perhaps from the first — behold this is double safek in itself and in mixture — one must say this case is different: there the widow has a presumption of kashrus and her daughter is in truth invalid; and even though Tosafot wrote Kesubos 14 s.v. "widow of dough," etc. that therefore the daughter is invalid — not by law, only they made an enhancement in lineage — this they wrote according to Rabbeinu Tam who validates all these double safeks. But according to R' Yochanan who disagrees — in truth the daughter is invalid by law, for there is no double safek at all; and this that R' Yochanan holds regarding an egg of safek tereifah that became mixed in a thousand that double safek does not help — the above that it is one safek in itself and one safek, etc. — even though an egg has a presumption of heter that it is not tereifah — one can say it deals with Rashi's explanation there that there are here two chickens — one kosher and one certainly tereifah — and they laid an egg and we do not know from which it came — if so presumption of heter does not apply here, for it is not known from which it was born — whether from tereifah or from kosher. And according to that view that Rama wrote — since the first safek is from the Torah, etc. — one can say this applies according to Rashba and Ran who hold every safek of prohibition from the Torah is forbidden — if so one can well say one should not combine it in the category of safeks of mixtures; but if it is forbidden only d'rabbanan — if so what of it that the first safek is forbidden from the Torah — this is itself to forbid it is d'rabbanan. And behold Rashba and Ran resolved according to his view that safek from the Torah is forbidden — why is safek mamzer and shetuki permitted from the Torah? For in lineage matters the Torah was lenient — accordingly one could say that even safek challal is included, which is not more stringent than safek mamzer; and if so, from the Torah its safek is permitted, and this safek joins the safek of mixture and it is a double safek, and it is not comparable at all to other safeks whose safek is forbidden from the Torah — investigate.
Double safek. And behold Pri Chadash brought Rabbeinu's view that he holds regarding d'rabbanan issur R' Yochanan concedes to R' Tam; and Pri Chadash challenged: behold R' Yochanan holds regarding the egg that the mishnah teaches "its safek is forbidden" and "it became mixed" — it deals with safek and not certainly; and from this he disagrees with R' Tam who holds safek in itself, etc.; we say: if so in the conclusion that we establish regarding born on Yom Tov alone — and it is only d'rabbanan issur; and nevertheless the mishnah teaches "it became mixed," etc. — learn that even regarding d'rabbanan issur we do not say safek in itself, etc. And I do not know what this great commotion is — granted if it deals with safek tereifah, R' Yochanan holds one cannot say "if it became mixed in a thousand" — certainly tereifah, certainly tereifah — who mentioned its name? Behold there is no mention in the baraita at all of certainly tereifah until the language can apply to it "and if it became mixed," etc.; and perforce it came out that the mishnah teaches "and its safek" — that is, safek tereifah is forbidden — deals with "and if it became mixed"; and R' Yochanan's words are correct. But if it deals with an egg born on Yom Tov — one can well say "and if it became mixed" — certainly born on Yom Tov deals with — for the baraita begins with an egg born on Yom Tov, etc.; and it deals well upon it that if this egg with which the baraita began — and that is born on Yom Tov — became mixed in a thousand — requires study that it deals with certainly; but regarding safek it is double safek and permitted — requires study.

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (שם אות ז') מ"מ הרי אנחנו באנו. לא זכיתי להבין דמ"ש מספק טריפה שנתערבה בחתיכות כשירות שהם חהר"ל ופירש א' מהם דאסור כמ"ש הש"ך בסמוך אות י' מכ"ש הכא דהוי קבוע דאורייתא לדעת הש"ך סקי"ד וט"ז וצ"ע:
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: (there letter 7) Nevertheless here we have arrived. I have not merited to understand what he wrote regarding doubtful tereifah that was mixed among kosher pieces which are chahal (pieces worthy of honor) and one separated that it is forbidden as Shach wrote nearby letter 10 — all the more so here where it is fixed d'oraisa according to Shach s.k. 14 and Taz — requires study:

nekudot_hakesef.he: (שם ס"ק ט') ואני אוסר כבודם במקומם מונח כו'. ודאי כבודם במקומם מונח דהמעיין בתוס' והרא"ש יראה לעינים דליכא איסור כלל כשאוכלם בזה אחר זה אפילו אדם אחד:
nekudot_hakesef.en: (there s.k. 9) And I forbid — their honor rests in their place, etc. Certainly their honor rests in their place, for one who examines Tosafos and Rosh will see plainly that there is no prohibition at all when eating them one after another, even one person:

kaf_hachayim.he: ט) ודבר חשוב האוסר בהנאה דמוכר חוץ מדמי איסור שבו ודאי דבעינן למכור הכל ביחד אבל למכור חדא חדא ולהשליך האחרון או ישליך הראשונה אסור דשמא לוקח דמי איסור הנאה משא"כ כשמכרן ביחד ומוזיל לגבי העכו"ם אותו של איסור. שפ"ד שם. זב"צ או' ו'.
kaf_hachayim.en: 9) And regarding an important item that forbids in benefit, which one sells except for the monetary value of the forbidden portion within it — it is certain that we require selling everything together; but to sell them one by one and discard the last, or discard the first, is forbidden, lest the buyer receive the monetary value of the benefit prohibition. Not so when he sells them together and discounts toward the non-Jew the portion of the prohibition. Shulchan Panim ibid. Zivchei Tzedek note 6.

kereti.he:
ונודעו היינו דב' ספיקות בגופו אבל אם היה רק חד בגופו רק לא נודע עד שנתוודע ספק בתערובות מכל מקום לא מהני כיון דחד בגופו ואחד בתערובות:
כגון עוף דין זה צ"ע כי אין קרוי חזקת איסור כי עוף בחזקת איסור לענין אמ"ה אבל לא לענין טריפות:
kereti.en:
"And they became known" — meaning that there are two doubts in its substance; but if there was only one in its substance and it only became known when a doubt in the mixtures became known, in any case it does not help, since one is in its substance and one in the mixtures.
Such as poultry — this law requires further study, for it is not called a presumption of prohibition, since poultry is in a presumption of prohibition regarding idolatrous slaughter, but not regarding treifah.

mechaber.he: ריאה טרפה שנמצאת בין ריאות כשרות ואמר הבודק שהי' יודע באות' סירכא ובשגגה נתערבו אותה ריאה טרפה בין הכשרות ולא היתה בכבשים ערבוביא הכבשים מותרים:
mechaber.en: A treifah lung that was found among kosher lungs and the examiner said he knew that adhesion and by mistake that treifah lung became mixed among the kosher ones, and it was not a random mixture of sheep — the sheep are permitted.

beer_hagolah.he: הרא"ש בתשוב' והרשב"א בת"ה והר"ן בפ"ז דחולין ממימרא דרבה בר אבהו א"ר נחמן טבעת של עובד כוכבים ומימרא דריש לקיש חבית של תרומה וכו' שם:
beer_hagolah.en: The Rosh in a responsum, the Rashba in Torat HaBayit, and the Ran in chapter 7 of Chullin — from the statement of Rabbah bar Avuhu, that R' Nachman said regarding a ring of a non-Jew, and the statement of Resh Lakish regarding a barrel of terumah, etc., there.

beur_hagra.he: ריאה כו'. דמעמידין הבהמות בחזקת כשרות כמו בכל ספק דמעמידין על חזקתה ואפילו באשת איש כמ"ש בפ' ד' אחין ל' ל"א ושאר מקומות וכ"ש כאן כמ"ש בפ"א דחולין ט' א' נשחטה בחזקת כו' הא קמ"ל כו' וכ"ש דע"א מעיד ועבה"ג:
beur_hagra.en: Regarding the lung, etc. — for we establish animals in a presumption of kashrus, as in every safek that we establish on its presumption; and even regarding a married woman, as written in chapter 4 of Yevamot (80, 11) and other places; and all the more so here, as written in the first chapter of Chullin (9a) "it was slaughtered in a presumption," etc. — behold it teaches us, etc.; and all the more so that one witness testifies, and in Beit HaGedolah.

pitchei_teshuva.he: [ כולם אסורים. עש"ך ס"ק נ"ב ועמ"ש אא"ז בעל פנים מאירות בחידושיו בזבחים שם וגם בתשובת חמדת שלמה סי' י"ח]:
pitchei_teshuva.en: [All are forbidden. Shach s.k. 52; and see what Or Zarua author of Panim Me'irot wrote in his chiddushim in Zevachim there; and also in responsa Chemdat Shlomo siman 18].

rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.he: (אות י"ח) כאיסור ודאי ע' בס' שער המלך (פ"א ה"ך מהל' י"ט):
rabbi_akiva_eiger_yd.en: (letter 18) Like a definite prohibition — see in Sefer Sha'ar HaMelekh (chapter 1 halacha 21 of Hilchot Yevamot):

nekudot_hakesef.he: (שם ס"ק י') ויש תימה על הש"ע דלעיל סי' זה ס"ד כו'. עי' בש"ך סקכ"ג ישוב לזה:
nekudot_hakesef.en: (there s.k. 10) And there is an astonishment on the Shulchan Aruch that above in this siman seif 4, etc. See in Shach s.k. 23 — resolution for this:

kaf_hachayim.he: י) ונראה אף שהעכו"ם יודע שמוזיל גבי שרי כיון שמה"ת חד בתרי בטל ומדרבנן הוא ומיהו אי לא בטיל חד בתרי (אלא חד בחד) דהוי איסור תורה יש לעיין ביה דשמא דוקא עכו"ם שאין מכירו מותר. שפ"ד שם.
kaf_hachayim.en: 10) And it appears that even when the non-Jew knows that he discounts [the price] regarding the permitted [items], since by Torah law one in two is nullified and it is rabbinic — nevertheless, if it is not nullified one in two (but rather one in one), which constitutes a Torah prohibition, this requires study — for perhaps specifically a non-Jew who does not know him is permitted. Shulchan Panim ibid.
